title: Bake simulations, closed-form springs
statement: Physics, cloth, particles with velocity and fluids are simulated once at a fixed 1/60 s step into a per-frame table that the render reads; springs use the closed-form solution, never a per-frame step.
evidence: pack determinism contract; the closed-form spring classes give identical values in forward and shuffled seek order in the type-module tests.

sources.locator: Things that break the rule: Simulation, Springs

notes: Set today by: type/ease.js spring / springTrack (SPRING classes) (a pack default outside mp plan). | Re-simulating from 0 on every seek also works but costs O(t) per frame. | Integration 21 Oct: lint.motion.seek is the static clock / random scan; it cannot see baking or preloading, so this rule has no lint check (the page seek test is motion-stack seekcheck.mjs, run by hand).

title: Lock the camera on impacts
statement: The camera does not move during a key action (drop, slam, snap, stamp): within those windows it stays under 0.8 deg/s orbit, 0.15 units/s distance and 0.8 deg/s roll; camera travel between zones takes at least 1 s.
evidence: rule carried from earlier 3D film builds; cam3d.lintCameraMoves reports violations and cam3d.lock freezes the camera over given windows.
notes: Tools that touch it today: camera/cam3d.js lintCameraMoves. Set today by: design.json motion.camera_still_on_impacts (a pack default outside mp plan). | lintCameraMoves is a library lint exercised in camera tests; no build gate calls it.

title: Cut effects peak on the cut
statement: Cut-synchronous effects (leak flash, chroma hit, bloom pulse) peak on the cut frame with about a 1-frame attack and 8-frame decay, and the next shot starts clean; at most one energy spike per beat.
evidence: binding compositing rule plus the shared envelope helper; on a 120 BPM grid the research allows a spike every 2nd beat in verses and every beat only in a drop.
notes: Set today by: type/ease.js env (attack, decay) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Declare audio; never play it live
statement: Sound reaches the render only as declared audio (an audio element with an id and a start time) or an offline master mix; live-playback audio never reaches the MP4.
evidence: Measured: a live-playback audio library produced no audio stream; a declared tag placed a 500 ms cue at 500.04 ms; the offline master held -14.1 LUFS through AAC within 0.1 LU.

sources.locator: Audio: declare it, or mix it offline

title: At most 3 flashes per second
statement: No more than 3 general or red flashes in any 1 s window (opposing luminance changes of 10% or more over 25% of the frame, darker side under 0.80).
evidence: WCAG 2.3.1 adopted as a pack rule; eyes synthetic tests: a 4 Hz full-frame strobe fails, 2-3 Hz passes.

sources.locator: Environment > Flash safety counts opposing luminance changes

notes: Set today by: design.json look.flash_max_per_s (a pack default outside mp plan). | An approximation of WCAG 2.3.1 (consecutive-frame changes, whole-frame area); not a broadcast Harding test. | Merged: No more than 3 general or red flashes per second (pairs of 10% relative-luminance changes over a quarter of the screen); space flash onsets at least 0.34 s apart. [house; published accessibility standard (WCAG 2.3.1).] | Also tools/a11y_check.py a11y/flash-plan. Use peak 0.7 for anything broadcast-adjacent.

title: Glitch only on hits
statement: Glitches trigger only on a beat or cut, last 4-8 frames, and occur at most once per 2 s; never run continuously.
evidence: effect-budget practice in the visual research; tone-cell guidance limits glitch to drops.
notes: Slice displacement 8-60 px, RGB split about 6 px.

title: Handheld is a sum of sines
statement: Handheld shake is a closed-form sum of seeded sines of t: slow position plus or minus 5 px at 0.37/0.83/1.31 Hz, micro plus or minus 0.8 px at 7.1/9.3 Hz, roll plus or minus 0.25 deg, scaled by level subtle 0.4, doc 1.0, action 2.5.
evidence: researched starting values, implemented in camera parts; determinism of the formula is tested.
notes: Set today by: camera/cam3d.js HANDHELD_LEVELS (a pack default outside mp plan). | Never noise stepped per frame; weave on film looks is 0.15% of W at 1-3 Hz and applies to the plate only.

title: Design the loop through frame 0
statement: A loop is designed, not cut: the last motion runs through frame 0, frame N equals frame 0, and the decoded seam difference (frame N-1 to 0) stays within 1.5x its neighbours plus 0.05.
evidence: 3 measured builds passed, e.g. decoded seam 0.811 against neighbours 0.752-0.787.

[house; platform spec: since 2025-03-31 Shorts counts a view on every start or replay [S]; the seam thresholds are house [H].] | skills/spec-to-loop/scripts/check_loop.py tests the seam against neighbouring frame diffs (seam <= 1.5 x max neighbour + 0.05), not SSIM 0.92; critic_pack reports loop_seam_psnr_db.

title: Clip masked rises to their start
statement: A masked line or character rise is clipped to its start time; shown before its start, the 1.12 em mask leaks the top 0.26 em of the glyphs.
evidence: Access lane found the leak in both renderers and the Lottie export; compositions hide it only because the clip starts at the entrance.

sources.locator: Findings for other lanes, maskRise bullet

notes: Related: mid-rise headline frames (about 3 per headline) can show stray punctuation of words still under their mask (saas lane, Weaker).

title: Barcode-check sourced media frames
statement: For anything with its own timeline (video, Lottie, sprite sheets, baked tables), burn a frame-index barcode or counter into the source and read it back at sampled frames; let the renderer own media playback.
evidence: in pack tests a video seeked with currentTime = N/fps showed the previous frame on 11 of 24 samples while still passing all three determinism gates.

sources.locator: Repeatable is not the same as right

notes: Repeatable is not the same as right: the seek gates prove purity, not correctness. | Merged: Content with a source timeline (video, Lottie, baked tables) also needs a frame-identity check such as a burned-in frame-index barcode, because a plain video element seeked to N/fps showed the wrong frame on 11 of 24 samples while passing G1-G3. [measured; Measured on 13 Oct 2026: renderer-owned video 300/300 frames exact; a hand-seeked video element one frame early on 11 of 24.] | Let the renderer own the video element; if you must drive it yourself, seek to (N + 0.5) / fps.

title: Morph one container instead of cutting
statement: Let one container change shape and meaning through the film (bar to circle to ball to bubble) instead of cutting; type-led films did this with 0-1 cuts.
evidence: 2 tier-A films used 0 cuts in 35 s and 1 cut in 15.5 s; the third tier-A film scaled and slid its prompt box but cut 6 times.

title: One signature camera move
statement: Use one signature camera move per film (a dolly zoom of about 2.4 s, fov 20 to 55, or a whip), and never mix handheld with a locked-off studio look in one piece.
evidence: camera practice in the visual research; dolly zoom keeps subject width via dist = D0 tan(fov0/2) / tan(fov/2).
notes: The move exists as a part; nothing counts signature moves.

title: Cap overshoot at 7%
statement: House motion overshoots at most 7%, settles in 3 bounces, anticipates 3-5 frames and delays secondary parts 2-4 frames; bigger springs are for playful (kinetic-soft) pieces only.
evidence: pack motion-character rule for props and characters; recorded in design.json motion.overshoot_max.

title: Pin render libraries; upgrades are projects
statement: Pin every rendering library's version per project and treat an upgrade as its own project (re-run the gates, re-grade), because moving three.js r160 to r186 darkened every lit surface by about 7/255.
evidence: Measured in the 3D lane of the 13 Oct 2026 bake-off (a +7.3% exposure re-grade would be needed after the bump).

title: Preload everything before ready
statement: Fonts (document.fonts.ready), images, models and HDRIs load before the page signals ready; nothing is fetched at seek time, and rendering uses a fixed pixel size with device scale factor 1.
evidence: pack determinism contract; lazy loads and font swaps fail the same_twice and cold_equals_warm gates.

notes: Text measured before fonts load lays out wrongly; give each animated property one owner timeline. | Integration 21 Oct: lint.motion.seek is the static clock / random scan; it cannot see baking or preloading, so this rule has no lint check (the page seek test is motion-stack seekcheck.mjs, run by hand).

title: Punch in 1.08-1.15 at sentences
statement: Talking-head punch-ins scale 1.00 to 1.08 or 1.15 in 6 frames (ease-out expo) on sentence boundaries, re-centred on the face, never two identical framings in a row, and at least 4 s apart.
evidence: practitioner retention heuristic in the visual research (marked to tune against real retention curves); coded as cam2d.punchCadence with lintPunchCadence.
notes: Tools that touch it today: camera/cam2d.js lintPunchCadence. | visual.md asks for any visible change every 2.5-3.5 s; lintPunchCadence demands 4 s between punch-ins, so other interrupts (cuts, graphics) must fill the gaps.

title: Every frame is f(t)
statement: Every pixel at time t is a pure function of t: seek(t) twice, forward/reverse/shuffled orders, and a cold seek to frame N all give identical pixels; a mismatch above about 60 dB PSNR is GPU noise, a real state bug measures 15-40 dB.
evidence: seek-test harness runs on the pack's library bake-off; preview-loop repaints measured 8-23 dB mismatches.

notes: Seek renderers may render frame 90 before frame 12 or one frame per worker; anything depending on wall clock or prior frames stutters or differs between renders. | Merged: Every pixel at time t is a pure function of t: the same frame twice, any seek order and a cold seek must match (gates G1-G3), where mismatches above 60 dB PSNR are GPU noise and below are state errors. [measured; 75 variants of 20 libraries measured across 5 lanes on 13-14 Oct 2026; clocks, rAF loops, live stepping and unseeded randomness failed the gates.] | Passing G1-G3 proves repeatability, not correctness; render through the real pipeline (G4) and look at stills from the delivered file. | Merged: Every part renders from t alone (no Date, no Math.random, no live springs, no caches that differ across processes), and determinism is proved on png-sequence frames (identical, or >= 60 dB where blurs add GPU noise), never by comparing MP4s. [house; house rule; own measurement: two default MP4 renders differ at about 44-50 dB from encoder noise though page frames are identical.] | Also tools/tests/xproc-hash.test.mjs (two fresh processes) and critic_pack det/report. GSAP needs force3D false and one warm pass; load fonts and images before the first frame. | Merged: A double render or seek test passes when every differing frame is >= 60 dB PSNR (GPU noise); the proof demo's worst frames measured 88.8-105.7 dB. [measured; Proof demo double png-sequence render of 1128 frames: worst PSNR 88.8 dB (16:9) and 91.0 dB (9:16), at most 2/255 per pixel; seek gates 96.4-105.7 dB.] | seekcheck prints 'FAIL (noise only, >= 60 dB)' for GPU blur noise; treat that as a pass for this bar.

title: Seeded randomness, never clock
statement: No Math.random, Date.now, performance.now, animation-frame deltas or timeout choreography: every random value is a seeded hash of (seed, frame or particle id, i), indexed by id and never by frame order.
evidence: pack determinism contract; order-dependence shows up as a failed order_independent gate.
notes: Seeded PRNGs named: mulberry32, sfc32, PCG hash.

title: Move by motion class
statement: Animate with closed-form stacked springs by class: UI snaps with about 1% overshoot, panels settle, the camera glides with none, headlines land hard (about 9%) and hold, mascots bounce.
evidence: Practitioner method from a round method article; overshoot values are the pack's implementation.
notes: Set today by: type/ease.js SPRING (ui, panel, camera, headline, mascot) (a pack default outside mp plan).

title: Whip pan: 7 f, cut mid
statement: A whip pan swings about 70 degrees over 7 frames with about 2 degrees of roll, hides the cut at peak velocity (the middle frame), and pairs with a chroma hit of about 10 px and a whoosh peaking on the cut.
evidence: researched starting values in the visual research, implemented as the whip parts (not tuned against references).
notes: 2D twin: cam2d.whip2d (dx 1.2, roll 1.5 deg).
